title: KV cache guardrails and poisoning detection
creator: Arjun Mehta
description: Follow-up work from a mid-February capacity/outage event where a small percentage of requests observed corrupted prefix entries leading to increased evictions and degraded tail latency. This ticket scopes preventive detection, emergency mitigations, stronger invariants, and monitoring to prevent recurrence without regressing latency or cost.
incident_summary: On 2025-02-14 we observed repeated eviction storms tied to malformed KV prefixes introduced during a batching path regression. The malformed entries bypassed existing checksum heuristics and caused slab mis-accounting which amplified memory pressure and triggered cascade evictions across shards, causing a 4.3x tail latency spike for affected models. Autoscaling partially absorbed throughput but could not stop error rates for 12 minutes.
root_cause: A regression in the LRU eviction path (PR #4578) changed the order of completion for batched writes. Under a narrow interleaving this produced truncated prefix keys with NUL bytes at the tail. These keys were not being scanned by the integrity sweeper because their header flag was set incorrectly by the new code path, and our checksum verification only ran on top-level writes, not on in-memory compacted shards.
remediation_summary: Short-term: revert the batching order change, re-enable conservative eviction thresholds, and scrub affected shards. Medium-term: harden write invariants, add prefix-level checksums and background scrubbing, introduce a canary mode for kernel changes, and add more granular telemetry for prefix integrity. Long-term: add deterministic e2e fuzz tests and a chaotic injection suite for cache operations.
action_items: A1: Patch revert and emergency rollout of batching-order fix. Owner: Emily Chen. Due: 2025-02-19. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4592
A2: Implement prefix-entry checksums and validate on read/write paths. Owner: Arjun Mehta. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2025-02-28. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
A3: Add background scrubbing job that detects truncated keys and tombstones, with definitive alert if >0.1% of entries flagged in 5m window. Owner: Sofia Alvarez. Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2025-03-05
A4: Improve telemetry: emit prefix-integrity metric, eviction-reason histogram, and shard-level memory-accounting drift gauge. Owner: Backend Observability. Due: 2025-02-24
A5: Canary rollout policy for kernel/ordering changes (start 5% traffic, automated rollback on integrity alerts). Owner: Platform. Due: 2025-03-01
A6: Add deterministic unit + integration tests covering NUL/truncated key cases and a small in-memory fuzz harness for batch interleavings. Owner: Testing Guild. Due: 2025-03-10
comments: 2025-02-14 - 10:12 UTC: Incident detected: eviction rate increase and tail latency spike for models served from shard group us-east-2-gpu-1. Pager duty routed to runtime oncall.
2025-02-14 - 10:25 UTC: Initial mitigation: raised eviction thresholds and bumped autoscale headroom for the cluster. Reduced request failures but not tail latency.
2025-02-14 - 10:48 UTC: Identified correlation between recent batching-order PR and malformed prefix keys in in-memory dump. Snapshot and artifacts uploaded to S3 and Confluence.
2025-02-15 - 09:00 UTC: Root cause confirmed via synthetic reproducer. Revert prepared and validated in staging.
2025-02-19 - 02:11 UTC: Emergency revert rolled out (PR #4592). Post-rollout monitoring shows integrity metrics returning to baseline. Follow-ups scoped in this ticket.
2025-02-20 - 15:30 UTC: Design review for checksum approach completed. Avoiding per-token hashing to keep latency impact minimal; using 64-bit rolling checksum on prefix header.
2025-02-22 - 11:05 UTC: Telemetry instrumentation merged for eviction reason and integrity counters; dashboards created and alert thresholds proposed. Pending runbook updates.
